subject: Trading
title: Sticking to the Stop-Loss
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sticking to the Stop-Loss.

hook.text: Your stop-loss is at $95. The stock hits $95.10. You move the stop to $90, hoping for a bounce. That's how ruin starts.

buildup.text: A stop-loss is a pre-set exit point designed to limit damage. Moving it further away defeats its purpose.

discovery.text: Moving stops wider turns a small, planned loss into an unplanned large one—the kind that devastates accounts.

twist.text: The pain of taking a small loss is real. But the pain of a blown account is permanent. Small losses are tuition.

climax.text: A stop-loss is a promise to your future self. Breaking it breaks your trading process.

punchline.text: Honor the stop. It's there for a reason.

quiz.question: Why is moving a stop-loss further away dangerous?
options: It turns a small planned loss into an unplanned large one
